title: Timebox slotting playbook: OKR-mapped tranches and rapid scope-cut decisioning
creator: Maya Chen
description: Playbook and lightweight tooling to slot initiatives into fixed timeboxes for the cycle, map each tranche to OKR outcomes, and enable fast, measurable scope cuts using a decision rubric. Intended to reduce mid-cycle churn, improve predictability for cross-functional staffing, and make scope-cut decisions defensible to stakeholders.
deliverables: Decision playbook PDF (timebox slotting + scope-cut rubric)
Cycle slot matrix (spreadsheet) mapping initiatives -> OKRs -> priority bands
Lightweight Slack slash command to register a scope-cut request (prototype)
Runbook for PM/Eng/Design daily intake during first 2 weeks of cycle
acceptance_criteria: Every active initiative has a named primary tranche (Anchor | Core | Buffer | Surge) and an OKR alignment tag
Scope-cut rubric yields a single recommended cut option within 24 hours for any flagged initiative
Staffing schedule shows role-level allocation per tranche with >=90% coverage for critical-path roles
Two dry-run decisions executed in the cycle planning rehearsal with stakeholder sign-off
work_items: Draft playbook document and one-page cheat sheet for leads
Create cycle slot matrix template and import current initiatives
Define quantitative triggers for reallocation (utilization, blocker counts, burn rate)
Prototype Slack slash command that files a scope-cut request to a triage channel
Run two planning rehearsals with Eng + Design leads and capture timings
Publish final playbook to Confluence and link in cycle kickoff deck
Train PM cohort on rubric and runbook in a 45-minute session
Add a field to PRD templates: primary tranche + OKR tag
milestones: 2026-03-01: Matrix template populated and rehearsals scheduled
2026-03-05: Tooling prototype (slash command) live in staging
2026-03-18: Playbook published and PM training complete
risks: Leads treat tranches as advisory rather than binding, reducing predictability
Quantitative triggers produce false positives during ramp weeks and cause unnecessary reshuffles
Design/Eng capacity estimates are optimistic leading to repeated mid-cycle cuts
Stakeholders request scope additions after tranche commitments are set
mitigation: Require a signed tranche commitment from leads in the cycle kickoff (email recorded)
Use a 48-hour debounce window on triggers during the first week of the cycle
Add a conservative 15% contingency buffer when calculating role-level hours
Introduce an 'exception gating' step where additions must be OKR-justified and approved by the cycle steward
notes: Timebox taxonomy: Anchor (must-deliver), Core (primary outcome), Buffer (nice-to-have, conditioned), Surge (opportunistic)
Scope-cut rubric tiers: 'Behavioral' (remove end-user flows), 'Surface' (UI polish), 'Integration' (non-critical infra), 'Docs/Telemetry'
Decision weighting: OKR impact (40%), customer-impact (25%), implementation effort (20%), risk to schedule (15%)
Example trigger: If critical-path role utilization > 85% for rolling 3 days AND unresolved blockers > 3 => trigger scope review
